rated_messages.input_message: Instead of smoking, use the next two minutes to pay close attention to your senses. Notice what you see, hear, feel, taste, and smell. Urges are just one part of your experience.

Spend 3 minutes noticing how your hands feel, how your mouth feels, and how your chest feels. The more you practice noticing these things without smoking, the sooner this place will stop being a trigger for you.
Notice how stress and anxiety may pull you and make you want to smoke. Just notice this. You can choose to just notice and not smoke.

Remind yourself that by staying quit, you'll be freeing yourself from the constant cycle of cigarette, nicotine withdrawal, feeling stressed as a result and wanting another cigarette. Keep going and this will be a thing of the past!
Try to avoid seeing other people smoke. It might sound basic but brain see, brain want! If you can, make life easier and avoid the people you used to smoke with for some time where possible.
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!
Think of your anxious mind like a toddler throwing a tantrum. The best way to respond is to quietly watch, but not give in.
Acknowledge your unhelpful thought by writing it down on a piece of paper. Then let it be on it's way by crumpling it up and tossing it in a trash can.
It can be tricky to be around friends or colleagues who are still smoking. If you're finding it tough, try and think about the things that you are doing well.

Don't let anyone tell you how you should or shouldn't feel today. You feel how you feel and that's it. If you're happy and grateful then enjoy the moment, if you're angry and frustrated, know that this will pass.
